Writing application logic using the Java activity method impacts maintainability, discourages reusability, and increases risk during upgrades. Use this method only when necessary. If executing Java code is required, consider using the Call-Function activity method to execute a Function rule. Using Function rules encourages creating well-defined input and output parameters and can be reused across many different types of rules.

Use of an internal activity from another ruleset is not recommended. The calling signature of these rules may change over time, or they may be deprecated completely. Consider using non-internal activities instead.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
Be careful not to write sensitive or confidential information, including encrypted properties and any properties from encrypted BLOBs, to logs.
